newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas seeks more shares for use in deals.
newsitem.headline: Adidas seeks more shares for use in deals.

text.p: German sportswear group Adidas AG said on Tuesday it would seek shareholder approval to raise seven million marks in nominal capital for possible use in acquisitions and sponsorship deals.

Adidas said in an advertisement for its annual general meeting in Germany's Boersen-Zeitung that sports associations that deal with Adidas have expressed interest in being paid in Adidas shares instead of cash for future deals.
The funds can also be used for employee share programmes, as initially approved in 1995.
The group, well known for its three-stripe logo, also said some of the funds may be used for acquisitions but did not elaborate in the announcement for its meeting on May 28.

Adidas, which is official sponsor of the 1998 World Cup, also said some associations had expressed interest in being paid in Adidas shares, whose price has more than tripled since an initial public offering in November 1995 to 185 marks.
"Foreign sports associations in particular and also some German associations have clearly expressed their interest in being paid in the form of shares," the advertisement said.
